Subject: ArcadiaMetrics — Deployment summary & next asks

Thanks again for the time today — quick summary and proposed next steps from our side. Please reply with clarifications or anything I missed.

High-level goals you shared
- Real-time anomaly scoring for telemetry events (sub-200ms p95 target end-to-end)
- Handle bursty traffic up to ~120 RPS for short windows, steady-state 35–50 RPS
- Model accuracy requirement: top-level classification/intent F1 >= 0.92 on your production labels
- Strong data controls: VPC-only, audit logs retained for 13 months

Primary pain points
- Current in-house model has inconsistent p95 (300–500ms) under burst; cold-starts are long
- Cost unpredictability during spikes; finance needs a predictable pilot cap
- Concerns about token leaks and auditability for regulatory customers

Redwood technical summary / recommendations (short)
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool in us-west-2) inside a customer VPC peering setup — meets your VPC & audit requirements
- Runtime: use a multi-variant routing policy: primary model = Llama-3-13B-optimized (int8-quantized) + fallback smaller variant for low-latency requests
- Caching: KV-prefix caching for repeated prefixes (expected 20–40% token reduction for your most common queries)
- Batching & latency: target batching window 10–15ms with continuous batching; expected p95 improvement to ~180–220ms in tests (depends on token length mix)
- Autoscale & burst: pre-warm pool for scheduled spikes + burst capacity routing to additional shared capacity if needed

Asks from Arcadia to size a pilot
1) 24h sample traffic capture (anonymized) with token length histograms
2) Security contact + completed security questionnaire (we can share our form)
3) A small labelled prompt set (50–100 examples) for quick quality validation

Next steps / owners
- Grace: Draft pilot scope + initial SOW and send to Tim by EOD Monday (attached: redwood-initial-sow-template.docx)
- Karthik: Run preliminary perf estimate based on traffic sample once received
- Jordan: Coordinate licensing/price band for a 3-month reserved pilot

Attachments: call-recording-20260515.mp3 (recording), redwood-initial-sow-template.docx (template)

Thanks — look forward to the technical deep-dive next week.

Best,

Thanks Grace — good summary. A few clarifications from our infra side:
- We run in AWS us-west-2 (EKS) behind an internal ingress with an NLB; we can peer with a vendor VPC or do VPC endpoints
- Typical token length is shorter for our event summaries (avg 40 tokens; 95th ~140 tokens)
- Current p95 (our homegrown endpoint) sits around 350ms under steady load and spikes to 600ms during batch ingestion windows
- Bursts are usually short (30–90s) but frequent during business hours; we need both predictable latency and a cost cap for pilots

Questions:
1) How does Redwood handle KV-cache invalidation for time-sensitive prefixes? We have many event IDs that should not be cached beyond a few seconds.
2) What telemetry do you expose for tracing token-level latency (we need to map to our APM)
3) Can you confirm fallback rules if the dedicated pool is saturated?

Attaching: arcadia-system-diagram.pdf (network topology)

We can do the deep technical session Tuesday 10am PT. Also Sara will send over our security contact details.

-Tim

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: ArcadiaMetrics — Deployment summary & next asks

Appreciate the diagram and details, Tim — quick technical notes in-line below and a proposed test plan.

KV-cache invalidation
- We support TTLs at the prefix level and explicit invalidation APIs; for highly time-sensitive IDs we recommend bypassing prefix cache or setting TTL <= 5s
- Also recommend a two-tier cache: short TTL on prefix + sticky session caching for high-rate users to avoid cold-starts

Telemetry / tracing
- We emit per-request token timing (start/end token wall clock), queue wait time, kernel execution time, and batch size in traces that can be forwarded to your APM (OpenTelemetry-compatible)

Fallback behavior when Dedicated pool saturated
- Controlled fallback routing: route to a compatible shared-hosted variant (smaller model) with probabilistic sampling to limit quality regression
- Canary: for first 10k requests we can route 95% to primary + 5% to fallback to verify latency/quality differential

Perf & topology proposal (for pilot sizing)
- Baseline: Llama-3-13B int8-quantized on 1x A100-like instance (dedicated runtime) with continuous batching (10–15ms window)
- Expected steady-state: 35–50 RPS at p95 ~180–230ms (dependent on token mix, we need the 24h capture)
- Burst handling: prewarmed pool of 2 extra instances and automatic scaling to 6 instances for peak windows (manual cap to control cost)
- Quantization option: Q4_0 gives best perf/quality tradeoff for your classification workload; we can A/B Q4_0 vs int8 on sample prompts

Proposed immediate test plan
1) Arcadia -> share 24h anonymized traces (token counts + timestamps) and 50 labelled prompts
2) Redwood -> run two 2-hour perf runs: (A) reserved-dedicated configuration; (B) dedicated + fallback routing enabled
3) Joint review: latency distribution, throughput headroom, and quality regression matrix

Estimated ballpark cost for pilot (3-week)
- Reserved pilot (dedicated + 24/7 prewarm): ~$18k–25k/month (depending on instance class & prewarm spec). We will provide a firm quote after the sample traffic run.

I can cover the technical deep-dive Tuesday; 10am PT works. I will bring a short perf checklist and test harness repo link during the call.

-Karthik
